records.text: Owens said Kelly Clarkson misunderstood the $15,000 price displayed for Molly: it referred to commissioning similar art, while the bird affixed to the Art of Play wall was not for sale.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: So she went to the store and she clearly, I think genuinely misunderstood when she saw Molly, the automated bird, which I have questions for why she wanted to own this. ... Okay, for $15,000, she saw $15,000 on the wall. And what they meant by that, which is you happen upon this in places that are artsy, is you can buy something similar to this. The artist's name is this. And for $15,000, they can make you a neon. ... You basically are commissioning art at that. ... At that point. And so she has a very quick back-and-forth with somebody who's probably making minimum wage and didn't treat her like the celebrity that she is, and told her that it wasn't for sale because it wasn't. It's affixed to their wall. It's obviously not for sale. Like, it's not like a shirt on a dummy. Actually, you can go to stores and a shirt on a dummy will not be for sale. They'll tell you that, and you just go, "Okay, it's not, that one's not for sale. It's the last one. We're not going to strip the dummy."
